The addition of WebMCP support for checkout, including Shop Pay, means these agents can now read the checkout screen, update it, and submit the transaction with the buyer's authorization, without relying on screenshots or scraping web pages, the company said. “If your agent is operating in the buyer’s browser, use WebMCP tools provided on storefront and checkout to efficiently complete order placement, instead of navigating HTML built for humans,” Greenberg wrote on X. “These WebMCP tools provide structured and efficient APIs, purposely designed — via UCP — to ensure accurate commerce facts, required disclosures, and handoff requirements.”

claims.claim: By allowing agents to finish checkout inside the buyer’s browser, Shopify expands the scope of agentic commerce while still requiring buyer consent before payment is submitted.
claims.bestSource: Shopify opens checkout to browser-based AI agents
claims.evidence: By explicitly blocking AI agents from handling payment credentials and requiring buyer consent before order finalization, Shopify has drawn a clear line that regulators and consumers can both understand. “If your agent is operating in the buyer’s browser, use WebMCP tools provided on storefront and checkout to efficiently complete order placement, instead of navigating HTML built for humans,” Greenberg wrote on X. “These WebMCP tools provide structured and efficient APIs, purposely designed — via UCP — to ensure accurate commerce facts, required disclosures, and handoff requirements.” OpenAI launched Instant Checkout on September 29, 2025, with Etsy sellers live in ChatGPT and more than a million Shopify merchants announced as coming soon, built on the Agentic Commerce Protocol it developed with Stripe.
